💡 What: Safely removed `HttpURLConnection.disconnect()` and implemented `try-with-resources` to cleanly consume both the `InputStream` and `ErrorStream`.

📊 Impact: Expected to reduce network latency significantly for subsequent URL shortening requests by bypassing the TCP handshake overhead.

## What changed

`update.sh`'s watchdog fires for two distinct failure modes:
1. `scanner.log` mtime stale (launchd stopped scheduling)
2. `scanner.log` fresh but no "Webhook OK" in the last 200 lines (crash-loop)

The beacon POST to `pugs-sales/api/sync/watchdog-fired` always sent `"reason":"scanner.log stale"` regardless of which mode triggered it — hardcoded on line 93.

When mode (2) fires, Charlie sees "scanner.log stale" in Vercel logs and investigates log staleness instead of the actual crash-loop. This is the wrong diagnostic and wastes triage time.

## Fix

Replace the hardcoded string with `$watchdog_reason` (set to the accurate description in each mode). Both failure modes now report their actual reason.

## Test

Added `update.sh: watchdog beacon body uses $watchdog_reason (not hardcoded "scanner.log stale")` to `src/update-sh.test.js`. This guards the regression: a future edit that hardcodes the reason again will fail the suite.

----

1e4a11482 was filtering on the cgroupv2 device to prevent a `cgroup_mount` variable with multiline content failing downsteam without clear errors.

cilium-originating mount

author: asheshgoplani
body:
Fixes #1407.

## The bug

Forked claude sessions inherited the parent's `ExtraArgs` only inside the baked one-shot fork command (built from the PARENT instance via `buildClaudeForkCommandForTarget`). The fork's own record never carried the tokens, so:

1. **First restart of a fork silently dropped the flags** — `buildClaudeResumeCommand` rebuilds from the fork's own (empty) `ExtraArgs`.
2. **Fork-of-a-fork never got them at all** — the fork builder reads its parent's persisted `ExtraArgs`, which was empty on a gen-1 fork.

By contrast `ClaudeOptions`-backed flags survived because `CreateForkedInstanceWithOptions` persists those via `SetClaudeOptions`. `ExtraArgs` was the only inherited piece not persisted.

## The fix

`CreateForkedInstanceWithOptions` persists an independent copy of the parent's `ExtraArgs` onto the fork (`append([]string(nil), i.ExtraArgs...)`), mirroring the existing `ClaudeOptions` persistence. The `len>0` guard keeps `nil` for parents without extra args so `omitempty` keeps `tool_data` clean. `ExtraArgs` is claude-specific; codex/opencode/pi fork paths are unaffected (this path forces `forked.Tool = \"claude\"`).

## TDD

`issue1407_fork_extraargs_test.go` — all red pre-fix, green post-fix:
- fork record persists the tokens + aliasing guard (independent copy) + **exactly-once** emission in the baked command (no double-emit)
- restart rebuild retains the flags (symptom 1)
- gen-2 fork inherits via the now-persisted gen-1 record (symptom 2)
- empty-parent stays `nil` (no-op guard)

Validated: `gofmt -l` clean, `go vet ./internal/session/` clean, full `internal/session` suite passes sandboxed.

body:
Completes the unattended inner loop up to the one remaining human gate: **the merge**. An agent can now take a task from issue → open, CI-green PR without permission prompts — branch off main, signed commit, push the branch, open the PR — while every mutation of `main` itself stays gated:

- `main` is branch-protected (verified), so a stray `git push` from main bounces server-side
- `gh pr merge` still prompts
- releases remain entirely human (release-please PRs are never agent-merged)

Deliberately scoped:
- `git push` (exact) and `git push -u origin *` only — no `--force`, `--delete`, or tag-push forms
- `git checkout main` (exact) + `git checkout -b *` + `git switch *` — plain `git checkout <ref>`/`git checkout -- <path>` (which can discard local changes) still prompts
- CI watchers remain report-only sentinels; this is the **maker** shipping its own branch, not the verifier touching what it watches

With this, the loop per PR is: edit → auto-format (hook) → `npm run verify` ×2 → branch/commit/push → PR → sentinel watches CI → human merges.

body:
## Add Aptos chain support

Adds Aptos as a supported chain to the omni-relayer, following the same MPC-proof-based finalization pattern used by Starknet.

### What's included

**New worker** (`omni-relayer/src/workers/aptos.rs`): handles all three event types —
- `process_init_transfer_event` — finalizes inbound Aptos→NEAR transfers using `NearFinTransferWithMpcProof`
- `process_fin_transfer_event` — claims relayer fee using `ClaimFeeWithMpcProofTx`
- `process_deploy_token_event` — binds token metadata using `BindTokenWithMpcProofTx`

**Indexer types** (`bridge-indexer-types`): adds `AptosTransaction` origin, `AptosInitTransferMessage`, `AptosFinTransferMessage`, `AptosDeployToken`, and `AptosLogMetadata` to the shared document types.

**Config**: new optional `[aptos]` section with `rpc_http_url` and `omni_bridge_address`; relayer account address read from `APTOS_ACCOUNT_ADDRESS`, private key from `APTOS_PRIVATE_KEY`.

**Dependency updates**: bumps `omni-types` and all `bridge-sdk-rs` crates to revisions that include Aptos support (`aptos-bridge-client` added).

### Known limitation

MPC finality is not currently wired to the EVM and Starknet bridge clients (it was previously). ## Le besoin, analysé

Il n'existe que **deux façons d'obtenir un siège** :

| Pattern | Cas | Token |
|---|---|---|
| **Auto-initié** | créer, rejoindre | dans la réponse HTTP (synchrone, déjà solide) |
| **Assigné** | matchmaking, **revanche** | le serveur t'assoit → il faut **naviguer** + **obtenir le token** |

La revanche suivait déjà un modèle propre pour « assigné » ; le matchmaking faisait autrement (push `match_found` portant le token), avec **un vrai trou** : la navigation dépendait du push, sans fallback durable. Push perdu → joueur matché **bloqué sur l'écran de recherche** (`wsLobby` ne rejoue rien à la reconnexion ; le commentaire qui prétendait le contraire était faux).

## La simplification : un seul modèle « assigné »

- siège **réservé par UserID, sans token** (`token_hash` NULL — ni le matcher ni `Rematch` ne génèrent de token) ;
- **navigation par signal durable** : revanche = event WS d'état (`rematchGameId`) ; matchmaking = **poll `GET /api/matchmake/current`** ;
- **token résolu par JWT à l'arrivée** (`resolveSeat`).

→ **Un seul chemin de creds** (résolution), **un seul modèle de navigation** (signal durable + hint instantané). Matchmaking et revanche deviennent le même flux.

## Serveur
- Sièges matchmaking **sans token** (plus de `newToken()` dans la transaction SQL — supprime un secret généré dans la couche repo). `MatchedSeat` = `{UserID, GameID}`. `match_found` = `{gameId}`.
- Nouveau `GET /api/matchmake/current` (`store.CurrentMatchmadeGame`) : partie publique non-terminée la plus récente où l'appelant a un siège. Pas de paramètre — le match est toujours la plus récente.

## Web
- `match_found` ne fait que naviguer ; les creds viennent de `resolveSeat` sur la page de jeu.
- `useMatchmake` **poll `/matchmake/current`** pendant la file (fallback durable) ; le son de match se joue une fois à la bascule.
- Commentaire mensonger supprimé.

## Tests
- `TestCurrentMatchmade_Contract` (auth + cas vide).
- Le chemin siège-sans-token → résolution → coup est déjà couvert par le test de résolution de revanche (désormais identique).
- Suite serveur + tsc + eslint + build web verts.

author: james-elicx
body:
## Impact

Externally reachable non-production App Router servers accepted a client-supplied `x-vinext-mw-ctx` header as trusted hybrid middleware state. An attacker could send `{}` to suppress real middleware execution, or provide an external rewrite URL to turn the dev server into an SSRF proxy, including forwarding POST bodies and attacker-provided credentials.

Normal `NODE_ENV=production` handling did not consume this bridge, but exposed development, preview, and shared internal servers were affected.

## Reproduction before this fix

Middleware bypass:

```bash
curl -i -H 'x-vinext-mw-ctx: {}' http://TARGET:3000/admin
```

Attacker-controlled POST rewrite / SSRF:

```bash
curl -i -X POST \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer attacker-controlled' \
  -H 'x-vinext-mw-ctx: {"r":"http://127.0.0.1:9000/probe"}' \
  --data 'sensitive-post-body' \
  http://TARGET:3000/admin
```

## Fix

- Treat `x-vinext-mw-ctx` as a vinext internal header and strip it at inbound request boundaries.
- Keep middleware result state exclusively in a bounded process-local registry stored under a `Symbol.for` key on the Node process object.
- Forward only a random, one-time, 30-second opaque handle between the hybrid Pages adapter and RSC environment.
- Atomically consume/delete handles before applying headers, status, rewrites, or proxying.
- Do not serialize secrets, trust material, middleware results, or registry access into the generated RSC virtual module.
- Preserve the hybrid behavior where middleware executes exactly once.

This follows Next.js's model of stripping client-supplied middleware control headers rather than trusting public request metadata.

## Security regressions

- Fetches all known Vite virtual-module URL forms and verifies no middleware trust material is disclosed:
  - `/@id/virtual:vinext-rsc-entry`
  - `/@id/__x00__virtual:vinext-rsc-entry`
  - `/@id/__x00__virtual%3Avinext-rsc-entry`
  - `/@id/%00virtual:vinext-rsc-entry`
- Client-supplied `{}` cannot skip middleware.
- Client-supplied rewrite context cannot trigger proxying.
- Forged POST rewrites cannot forward authorization headers or request bodies.
- Registry handles are one-time and cannot be replayed.
- Trusted hybrid context is accepted without running middleware twice.
- `x-vinext-mw-ctx` remains covered by vinext internal-header filtering.

## Validation

```bash
vp test run tests/app-middleware-context-security.test.ts tests/app-router-middleware-context-security.test.ts
vp test run tests/request-pipeline.test.ts -t "filterInternalHeaders"
PLAYWRIGHT_PROJECT=app-router pnpm run test:e2e -- tests/e2e/app-router/middleware.spec.ts -g "middleware runs exactly once"
vp check packages/vinext/src/server/dev-middleware-context-registry.ts packages/vinext/src/server/headers.ts packages/vinext/src/server/app-middleware.ts packages/vinext/src/server/app-rsc-handler.ts packages/vinext/src/entries/app-rsc-entry.ts packages/vinext/src/index.ts tests/request-pipeline.test.ts tests/app-middleware-context-security.test.ts tests/app-router-middleware-context-security.test.ts
```

All targeted tests and checks pass.

body:
Part of #11 (tree-rebuild slice).

## Problem

`AnalyticalModelControl.LoadAnalyticalModel` rebuilds the **entire** model tree — spaces → panels → apertures, plus shades, profiles, materials, internal conditions, mechanical systems and zones — from scratch on **every** reload. The perf log shows this at **~250–320 ms** on a large model (625 spaces), and it ran even when the edit couldn't have changed any of that content.

## Change

A pure `ViewSettingsModification` (Hide, colour, legend, camera — see `Modify.Hide` → `new ViewSettingsModification(...)`) only touches per-view settings; it never changes the spaces/panels/ICs/etc. that the model tree renders. So `LoadModel` is now **skipped** when *all* modifications are `ViewSettingsModification`.

Still rebuilds (unchanged behaviour):
- first load (empty tree), `Open`/`Close` events,
- any `FullModification` or `AnalyticalModelModification` (model genuinely changed).

`LoadViews` always runs (it's cheap, and a view rename does change it).

## Why it's safe

If every modification is a `ViewSettingsModification`, the model objects `LoadModel` reads are byte-identical, so the rebuilt tree would be identical — skipping is invisible. The skip is gated to never apply on open/close or model/full changes.

## Effect

- **Hide / colour / legend / camera** edits no longer pay the ~300 ms model-tree rebuild.
- **Renaming a space** (an `AnalyticalModelModification`) still rebuilds — its tree header must change. A targeted header-update for that case is a possible follow-up.

## To test

1. `SAM_UI_PERFORMANCE_LOG=1`, open a large model.
2. **Hide a space / change a colour** → `AnalyticalModelControl.LoadAnalyticalModel` should be **absent** from that reload (or near-0), and the model tree should look unchanged and stay correctly expanded.
3. **Rename a space** → tree still rebuilds and shows the new name (expected).
4. **Open / close / add / delete** a space → tree rebuilds correctly.
5. Confirm tree selection, double-click-to-edit, and drag-drop still work after a skipped rebuild.

Since smm-asset.pc now declares Requires.private: libcurl jansson tidy — which pkg-config resolves even for --cflags — consumers without the curl/jansson/tidy dev packages got "Package 'libcurl' ... not found" (verified in a trixie container).

Split into libsmmasset0 (runtime, named for the soname, dependencies generated by dpkg-shlibdeps) and libsmm-asset-dev (header, .so symlink, smm-asset.pc, depending on libsmmasset0 and the three dev packages). Both Break/Replace the old libsmm-asset so in-place upgrades from locally built 0.x debs do not hit file conflicts. Stop shipping the libtool archive, drop debian/rules' dead stretch/bionic special case and the redundant --with autoreconf (default in compat 13), replace the generator placeholders in debian/copyright with the project's actual LGPL-2.1+ statement, and ignore dpkg-buildpackage artifacts.

Validated in debian:trixie: builds with the declared Build-Depends, package contents and dependency metadata correct, and a consumer program compiles via pkg-config and runs against the installed split packages.

## Summary by Sourcery

Split Debian packaging into separate runtime and development library packages and clean up packaging metadata and artifacts.

Build:
- Introduce libsmmasset0 runtime and libsmm-asset-dev development Debian packages with appropriate dependencies and Breaks/Replaces on the legacy libsmm-asset package.
- Adjust Debian packaging rules to stop installing the libtool archive and remove obsolete special-case build logic.
- Update Debian copyright metadata to reflect the actual LGPL-2.1+ license statement.

Chores:
- Extend .gitignore to exclude dpkg-buildpackage artifacts from version control.

First slice of CyclesEvidence envelope emission (the long-pole gating `aeoess/agent-passport-system#43` (b), `runcycles/cycles-protocol#103`, and the `replay_class` decision_replay→full_replay promotion). **Foundation only** — the canonicalization + signing primitives, fully validated against the reference fixtures. Not yet wired into the dispatch path.

## What

New package `io.runcycles.events.evidence`:
- **`CyclesEvidenceCanonicalizer`** — the `cycles-evidence-v0.1` normative recipe: `evidence_id = sha256(JCS(envelope, evidence_id="" + signature=""))`; signing-input = `JCS(envelope, evidence_id populated + signature="")`. RFC 8785 via `io.github.erdtman:java-json-canonicalization:1.1` (the reference impl shared with the JS/Python JCS).
- **`EnvelopeSigner`** — Ed25519 sign/verify on the JDK-native EdDSA provider (no third-party crypto); raw 32-byte hex keys wrapped in fixed Ed25519 SPKI/PKCS#8 DER prefixes; fail-closed `verify`.

## The proof that matters

`CyclesEvidenceCanonicalizerTest` reproduces **all 13** `cycles-evidence-v0.1` reference fixtures' `evidence_id` **byte-for-byte** AND verifies their embedded signatures against `signer_did`, plus a sign/verify round-trip and fail-closed guards — **15/15**. This resolves the #1 risk: the Java JCS + JDK Ed25519 stack now agrees with the Python generator (`jcs` + PyNaCl) and the APS JS verifier byte-for-byte.

## Scope boundary

No dispatch-path wiring, no envelope storage/serving, no signing-key provisioning — those land in subsequent stacked slices. No wire change; no spec change (`cycles-evidence-v0.1` is schema-only and already authoritative). AUDIT.md updated.

## Summary Implements HANDOVER §5.4: a one-shot resumable EPSS history backfill job that populates the `epss_history` table for every CVE already in the DB using the FIRST API `scope=time-series` endpoint. Once complete it sets the `epss_backfill_done` marker in `sync_state` and never runs again; it is safe to restart mid-run (no duplicate rows). --- ## Changes ### `backend/feeds/epss.py` - Add `BACKFILL_BATCH_SIZE = 100` and `BACKFILL_THROTTLE_SECONDS = 2.0` (module-level constants) - Add `fetch_epss_time_series_batch(cve_ids)`: calls `https://api.first.org/data/v1/epss?cve=…&scope=time-series` for up to 100 CVEs in one request; returns `[{"cve_id", "score", "date"}]`; handles `CircuitOpenError`, HTTP errors, malformed items, and non-dict JSON responses; records one `api_usage` call per batch ### `backend/database.py` - Add `EPSS_BACKFILL_DONE_KEY = "epss_backfill_done"` - Add `get_sync_state_value(db, key)` — generic `sync_state` reader (returns `None` when absent) - Add `set_sync_state_value(db, key, value)` — generic `sync_state` upsert (caller commits) - Add `insert_epss_history_rows(db, rows)` — bulk `INSERT OR IGNORE INTO epss_history`; skips `(cve_id, recorded_date)` pairs already present; returns count of rows written ### `backend/scheduler.py` - All new imports added at module level (no inline imports per §7) - Add `_epss_backfill_lock = asyncio.Lock()` - Add `run_epss_backfill()` / `_run_epss_backfill()`: - Opens **one** DB connection for the entire job lifetime; released in `finally` - Reads `epss_backfill_done` marker → exits immediately if already set - Loads all CVE IDs from DB (only CVEs already present — no full archives) - Processes in batches of 100 with 2 s sleep between batches (≈ 30 req/min, well below 1 000/min limit) - Uses `INSERT OR IGNORE` — restart-safe, no duplicate rows - Sets `epss_backfill_done = "1"` only after all batches succeed - On any exception: logs error, releases connection via `finally`, returns without setting marker → retries on next startup - Wire into `maybe_run_on_startup()` via `asyncio.create_task(run_epss_backfill())` ### `backend/tests/test_epss_backfill.py` *(new — 16 tests)* | Group | Tests | |---|---| | `fetch_epss_time_series_batch` | Parse response, uppercase normalisation, malformed item skipping, empty input, circuit-open → empty, HTTP 500 → empty, non-dict JSON → empty | | `insert_epss_history_rows` | Inserts new rows, ignores duplicates, empty input | | Sync state helpers | `get_sync_state_value` / `set_sync_state_value` round-trip | | `run_epss_backfill` | Marker-skip (no API calls), happy path (rows + marker set), idempotency (no duplicate rows on second run), marker set after completion, concurrent-call skip | All use in-memory SQLite + `httpx.MockTransport` — no live server, no real API calls. --- ## Compatibility - **Additive only**: no existing tables, columns, or endpoints changed - **No migration needed**: `epss_history` and `sync_state` already exist - **No env vars added**: batch size and throttle are hardcoded constants (sensible defaults, not operator-tunable) - **Idempotent**: `INSERT OR IGNORE` + marker prevents any side effect from repeated runs --- ## Test run ``` cd backend && pytest tests/ -q 154 passed, 6 warnings in 8.1s # baseline 138 + 16 new ``` --- ## Post-merge verification Run these on the production box after `bash deploy/briefr-update.sh`: ```bash # 1. Universal 30-second smoke bash /opt/briefr/deploy/check-backend.sh journalctl -u briefr-backend --since "-5 min" -p err # expect empty curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/health | python3 -c \ "import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin); print(d['status'], d['cve_count'])" curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/version # commit must match deployed HEAD # 2. Confirm backfill job started (appears within seconds of restart) journalctl -u briefr-backend --since "-5 min" | grep -i "epss backfill" # expect: "EPSS history backfill started at ..." # 3. Watch row count grow (check again ~60s later) sqlite3 /opt/briefr/backend/briefr.db \ "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM epss_history; \ SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT cve_id) AS cves_with_history FROM epss_history;" # 4. After backfill completes, verify marker is set sqlite3 /opt/briefr/backend/briefr.db \ "SELECT key, value, updated_at FROM sync_state WHERE key='epss_backfill_done';" # expect: epss_backfill_done|1| # 5. Confirm sparklines have >1 data point for an older CVE (e.g. Log4Shell) curl -s "http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/cves/CVE-2021-44228/epss-history?days=30" | \ python3 -c "import json,sys; h=json.load(sys.stdin); print(len(h), 'history points')" # expect: >= 2 history points # 6. Confirm idempotency: restart the service; marker should prevent re-run sudo systemctl restart briefr-backend journalctl -u briefr-backend --since "-2 min" | grep -i "epss backfill" # expect: "EPSS backfill: marker 'epss_backfill_done' already set — skipping" # 7. Confirm no new errors in journal journalctl -u briefr-backend --since "-2 min" -p err # expect empty ```

## Summary
Complete the MVP by wiring all components into a working FastAPI server.
Adds configuration management, structured logging, dependency injection,
and the public REST API.

## Why
Previous PRs added internal components (models, store, handlers, worker)
but none were exposed externally. This PR makes the system reachable from
HTTP clients and runnable as a server.

## Changes
- **`config.py`** — `Settings` class loading from `.env` (host, port, log_level)
- **`logging.py`** — structlog config emitting JSON logs
- **`api/deps.py`** — singleton `TaskStore` and `TaskWorker` shared via `Depends`
- **`api/routes.py`** — 4 endpoints:
  - `POST /tasks` — submit task (202 Accepted)
  - `GET /tasks/{id}` — get task (404 if missing)
  - `GET /tasks` — list with `status` and `task_type` filters
  - `DELETE /tasks/{id}` — cancel PENDING task (409 if running)
- **`main.py`** — FastAPI app + `lifespan` that starts/stops the worker
  alongside the server. Adds `/health` for liveness checks.

## How to test
```bash
uv run uvicorn task_queue.main:app --reload
```

Open http://localhost:8000/docs and try the endpoints, e.g. POST a
multiply task:
```json
{"task_type": "multiply", "payload": {"a": 6, "b": 7}}
```

Then GET the returned `id` — `status` should be `COMPLETED` with
`result: {"product": 42}`.

author: kennguy3n
body:
## Summary

S4 deliverable: a real Vite + React + TypeScript admin console under `web/console/`, wired to the kseal server over **Connect-Web** with clients generated from the canonical protos. Every page is implemented and calls a generated client — no stubs. `npm run build`, `npm run lint`, `npm test` (30 tests) and `docker build` are all green locally.

> Note: until the foundation branch merges to `main`, this PR's diff also shows foundation files; that is expected and self-corrects on merge. All of *my* changes live under `web/console/**`. This PR also has a soft dependency on the canonical `QueryService` proto (PR #6) — suggested merge order #5 → #6 → #4.

### What's here

- **Auth + transport** (`src/api/`): a Connect transport whose interceptor attaches `Authorization: Bearer <apiKey>` to every call. The key is read **lazily per call** from a ref, so re-login doesn't rebuild the transport. API key + tenant id + base URL persist in `localStorage`; the key is never logged.
- **Tenant isolation**: every RPC is `tenant_id`-scoped and react-query cache keys embed the tenant id, so caches can't bleed across tenants (designed for ~5000 SME tenants — logical isolation, no per-tenant schemas). The query cache is also `clear()`ed on both login and logout.
- **Pages** (all real, all wired): Login, Dashboard (overview + recent events + trust stats), Apps list, App detail (builds / active policy / recent events), Policy editor (author + activate), Events (filter by type / risk / time), Webhooks (list / create / delete).
- **Codegen**: `npm run proto:gen` runs `buf generate` directly against the canonical `//proto` buf module (owned by another component, never modified) into `src/gen/`. Generated output is committed so the Docker build (context = `web/console/` only) needs no access to `//proto`.
- **NoOps runtime config**: `VITE_KSEAL_API_BASE_URL` is inlined at build; the image *also* renders `/env.js` from `KSEAL_API_BASE_URL` at container start (nginx `/docker-entrypoint.d`) so one prebuilt image is configurable per deploy. Resolution precedence:

  ```
  window.__KSEAL_ENV__.apiBaseUrl   // runtime env.js (deploy-time)
    || VITE_KSEAL_API_BASE_URL      // build-time inlined
    || "http://localhost:8080"      // dev default
  ```

### Read surface — `QueryService` (now canonical)

The Dashboard overview and Events pages read derived data-plane state via `QueryService` (`ListEvents`, `GetTenantOverview`, `GetTrustSessionStats`). This contract was promoted into the canonical `//proto/kseal/v1/query.proto` + `query_service.proto` (PR #6) and implemented server-side with tenant-isolated, keyset-paginated queries. The console now:

- generates straight from `//proto` (the console-local `web/console/proto/` vendor copy was deleted);
- splits the generated output as canonical does — messages in `query_pb.ts`, the service in `query_service_pb.ts`;
- renders **real data** on those pages; `ErrorNotice` is now a thin transient-error fallback (the `Unimplemented` "pending support" degrade path was removed).

Event-type / risk-level chips are still refined **client-side** for instant toggles; only the coarse time range hits `ListEvents`.

### Keyset pagination (Apps / Builds / Events)

The three list-backed views now consume the server's keyset cursor instead of a one-shot capped page. `useApps`, `useBuilds`, and `useEvents` are `useInfiniteQuery` hooks that thread the response `next_page_token` back as the next request's `page_token`; a shared `<LoadMore>` control appends the next page and hides itself once the cursor is exhausted:

```ts
useInfiniteQuery({
  queryKey: queryKeys.events(tenantId, args),
  queryFn: ({ pageParam }) => listEvents({ ...args, pageToken: pageParam }),
  initialPageParam: "",
  getNextPageParam: (last) => last.nextPageToken || undefined,  // "" => stop
  select: (data) => data.pages.flatMap((p) => p.items),         // pages stay flat for callers
});
```

`select` flattens pages to a plain array, so page components keep reading `query.data` as before and just gain `hasNextPage` / `fetchNextPage`. Tenant-scoped cache keys and mutation invalidation are unchanged. This removes the previous silent truncation at the hard-coded page sizes.

### Security hardening (nginx)

- **CSP `connect-src` is tightened at container start.** `docker-entrypoint.sh` derives a strict `scheme://host[:port]` origin from `KSEAL_API_BASE_URL` and rewrites the CSP to `connect-src 'self' <origin>;`. It falls back to `*` only when the var is unset (build-time-configured deploys) or fails strict origin validation, so a malformed/hostile value can never break out of the directive.
- **Uniform security headers.** CSP, `X-Content-Type-Options`, `Referrer-Policy`, `X-Frame-Options` moved into a shared `nginx-security-headers.conf` snippet `include`d by every `location` (nginx does not inherit `add_header` into a location that sets its own), so `/`, `/assets/`, and `/env.js` all carry them. The runtime-config XSS vector (operator-controlled `KSEAL_API_BASE_URL` in `env.js`) is escaped at render time.

### Tests (Vitest + RTL, 30 passing)

- `api/transport.test.ts` — bearer header injection, absence when no key, lazy per-call read.
- `api/clients.test.ts` — end-to-end wiring through `createRouterTransport`, asserting the auth header reaches the handler and a client exists for every service.
- `lib/policy.test.ts` — `parsePolicyForm` validation and `parseModules` dedupe.
- `lib/events.test.ts` — `filterEvents` (type/risk AND-semantics, inclusive time range), `sortEventsByTimeDesc` stability.
- `pages/Events.test.tsx` / `pages/PolicyEditor.test.tsx` — component-level filtering, policy submission/validation, and **"Load more" pagination** (second page appended via `next_page_token`, control disappears when the cursor is exhausted) against a stubbed transport.

## Summary

Adds a draft ADR for connecting the existing local `runt mcp` server directly to hosted notebook rooms such as `https://preview.runt.run/n/<id>`, instead of requiring one MCP registration per notebook or relying on a remote MCP facade.

The ADR records:

- `connect_notebook(target=...)` as the preferred addressable entrypoint while preserving `path` and `notebook_id` compatibility.
- Hosted notebook URLs and remote aliases as room locators, not MCP resource URIs.
- A separate machine-local remote registry for hosted origins and credential references, rather than putting API keys into synced settings.
- Principal/operator handling: principal comes from the credential, operator comes from local config, and live Automerge actors still need nonce/persistence protection.
- The separation between document access and workstation/runtime attachment.
- Rejoin and parked-session implications for remote room targets.

## Why

This is the next likely foundation for agent collaboration against cloud notebooks: a local stdio MCP process should be able to sync directly with the hosted Automerge document set using local credentials and operator attribution.

## Review focus

- Does the settings/config split match the existing synced settings model?
- Is the target-resolution model compatible with current `connect_notebook` semantics?
- Are the principal/operator and actor uniqueness constraints stated clearly enough?
- Are the non-goals strict enough to avoid drifting into remote MCP or workstation authority changes too early?

author: jamesarich
body:
## Problem

`NodeTest.isOnline_usesStrictThresholdBoundary` is flaky on loaded CI (observed failing in #5760's shard-core, both `jvm` and `androidHostTest` variants), independent of any Kotlin version.

The test reads the clock twice. It computes `val threshold = onlineTimeThreshold()` once, then asserts `Node(lastHeard = threshold + 1).isOnline` — but the `isOnline` getter calls `onlineTimeThreshold()` *again*. `onlineTimeThreshold()` returns second-granularity epoch from a fresh `Clock.System.now()` on every call, so if the wall clock crosses a one-second boundary between the two reads, the assertion degenerates to `N+1 > N+1` and fails.

## Fix

Add an internal `isOnline(threshold: Int)` overload on `Node`; the public `isOnline` property delegates to it unchanged. The test now pins a single `threshold` for both the node construction and the check, eliminating the double clock read while keeping the strict `>` boundary assertion intact (no "add slop" widening, which would defeat the test's purpose).

This pull request introduces several documentation improvements and a key change to how vector index dimension mismatches are detected and handled in the Neo4j store. The main focus is to make the embedding pipeline more robust when switching embedding models, provide better guidance in the docs, and add corresponding tests for the new index dimension check.

**Key changes:**

### Neo4j vector index dimension handling

* The pipeline now checks for dimension mismatches between existing Neo4j vector indexes and the current embedding model. If a mismatch is detected, a clear `RuntimeError` is raised, instructing the user to drop and recreate the indexes. This prevents silent errors when switching embedding models with different output dimensions. author: 01laky
body:
The persistence version per `prompt/v0.6.0.md` (proposal §3, §5, §6) — **Level 1 is functionally complete and the L2 persistence lands with it**: the statistics survive restarts and are shared across clients.

## What's inside

- **The §6 model:** one table, atomic counters, no event log. Every conversion writes ONE `TransactWriteItems` with two `Update ADD`s (the global `conversionCount`/`totalEurCents` + the per-target counter) — both or neither, the global count can never drift from the target sum; no read before write.
- **Integer EUR cents at write time:** `from = EUR` → `Math.round(amount × 100)` directly, **no rate lookup** (a spy proves it); other currencies through `rate(from→EUR)` from the same cached payload, rounded once by `roundMoney`.
- **A conversion never fails because of statistics:** the WHOLE statistics step (the EUR leg AND the write) runs in one try/catch; the write retries ×3 with an injectable backoff; transient attempts log `warn` through the request-scoped logger (the retry lines carry the request id), the final failure logs `error` — and the 200 goes out regardless. Both failure paths tested.
- **`GET /api/stats`:** one Query; ties resolve to the alphabetically FIRST currency with a single strict-`>` pass over the Query's ascending sort-key order — no sort needed; `totalConversions` is a nonnegative **integer** in the OpenAPI contract; `topTargetCurrency` is nullable (the honest empty state); the response carries **no cache headers of any kind**.
- **A five-findings human prompt review** (recorded in the AI diary) shaped all of the above before a single line of code: the cents-vs-euros EUR branch, the two-legged try/catch, the free tie-break, the explicit schema types and the two-level retry logging.
- **Tests:** 15 new (95 total) — the repository against the real dynamodb-local (transactional totals, the tie-break, the empty state, the retry warn counts, the exhausted-retry throw) and the **end-to-end persistence proof**: `POST /api/convert` → `GET /api/stats` through the real database, green on the first run.

## Definition of done

All 6 prompt checkboxes ticked; `verify:api` green (typecheck + lint + 95/95 tests); `openapi.json` re-exported after the version bump; CHANGELOG `[0.6.0]` + version match; two diary records (the five-findings review + the implementation, including one honest stumble: a type-hack test the hook rejected, replaced with a clean `vi.spyOn`).

author: rhonstin
body: ## What Adds a **sampled-verify** mode to the qwen35 chain spec-decode path, enabled with `DFLASH_SAMPLED_VERIFY=1`. It implements the "active sampler during verification" item from the README's future additions: speculative decoding that works at **any temperature** while preserving the exact target sampling distribution. Today the chain verify commits the target's argmax at each position, so spec decode is only distribution-correct at temperature 0 — sampling requests fall back to AR decode. On a 27B Q4_K_M / RTX 3090 that means 16 tok/s for any agent traffic that samples. ## How it works Sample-and-match: at each chain position the verifier draws a token from the target's **full sampler chain** (temperature / top-k / top-p / penalties) over that position's verify logits, and accepts the draft token iff the sample matches it. On mismatch, the sampled token itself becomes the bonus token. Every committed token is therefore an exact sample from the target distribution — output distribution identical to AR sampling, no acceptance-rate correction terms needed. Three spots must sample rather than take argmax — each one, when wrong, corrupts generation in a distinctive way that we hit and fixed during validation: 1. **First token after prefill** — was the prefill argmax; injects one greedy token per request (at temp 1, 150/150 generations opened with the same word). Now sampled from the prefill logits. 2. **Per-step seed** — the next draft step is seeded with the replay's last token, which the next verify commits as-is. Argmax here injects one greedy token per step (~1/16 of output) and locks long generations into repetition loops. Now sampled from the replay's last verify logits. 3. **The acceptance walk** — over per-position verify logits, exposed via a new `DFlashTarget::read_verify_logits()` hook (virtual, default `false`; the qwen35 target reads the step graph's logits tensor, so targets that don't implement it are unaffected). ## fa-window interaction Sampled-verify is gated to `fa_window == 0`. With a finite `--fa-window`, the windowed **verify** pass starves the logit tail at long context: argmax survives, but sampling from the poisoned tail degrades quality. Decisive experiment on a 24K-token agent prompt: tool-call success **0/12** with a finite window vs **12/12** with full-attention verify. Prefill and AR decode always run full attention, so they're unaffected — this only constrains the verify pass. ## Results (RTX 3090, Qwen3.6-27B Q4_K_M + DFlash draft) | Workload | AR sampling | sampled-verify | |---|---|---| | short prompts, temp 0.7–1.0 | 16 tok/s | 60–70 tok/s | | 24K agent prompt w/ tools, temp 1.0 | 16 tok/s | ~31 tok/s | | tool-call success (12 runs, temp 1.0) | 12/12 | 12/12 | - Greedy path (`DFLASH_SAMPLED_VERIFY` unset) is bit-exact unchanged. - Token histograms over 150 sampled generations match AR within noise. - No degeneration over 1200-token continuous generations. - `DFLASH_SV_DEBUG=1` traces the acceptance walk per position. Default is **off**, so existing deployments see zero behavior change.

body:
## Summary

针对每请求都全量重写 `config.json` 的问题做了两处改造:

1. **原子写**：`Save()`（以及新的 state 写入）改为写同目录临时文件 → `fsync` → `rename` 覆盖。`rename(2)` 在同一文件系统内是原子的,杜绝进程崩溃/掉电时把存有 refresh token 的 `config.json` 写成截断/损坏文件。

2. **运行时 state 拆分**:把每请求高频变动的计数器从 `config.json` 移到同级的 `config.state.json`:
   - 每账号:`requestCount / errorCount / lastUsed / totalTokens / totalCredits`
   - 每 API key:`tokensUsed / creditsUsed / requestsCount / lastUsedAt`
   - 全局:`totalRequests / successRequests / failedRequests / totalTokens / totalCredits`

   这些字段在 Go 结构体上保留(admin 面板和 pool 仍读内存副本),但打上 `json:"-"` 不再进 `config.json`。热路径写计数器只刷 `state.json`,且在释放 `cfgLock` 之后再落盘,读配置的请求不再被统计写盘阻塞。

### 设计要点
- `state.json` 在 flush 时**从 cfg 派生**,不维护并行结构 ⇒ 删除账号/API key 并 flush 会自动丢弃其计数器,无孤儿残留(满足"删账号也删 state"的要求)。
- flush 由 `flushLock` 串行化,每次快照最新 cfg,并发写不会落盘旧值。
- 锁序固定 `flushLock → cfgLock`,热路径持锁期间不碰磁盘。

### 兼容/迁移
- 旧 `config.json` 仍带内联计数器时,首次启动一次性迁移进 `state.json`,并重写 `config.json` 去掉这些字段。
- 每个 config(含多实例部署)有独立的 `<name>.state.json`,靠 `CONFIG_PATH` 隔离。
- `/data/` 已在 `.gitignore`,新 state 文件自动覆盖。

## Test plan

- [x] `go build` / `go vet` 通过
- [x] `go test ./config` 全绿,新增 `config/state_test.go` 覆盖:state 落盘而非 config、重启 round-trip 恢复、删账号/删 key 丢弃 state、旧 config 内联计数器迁移
- [x] `go test ./...` 与基线对比:仅 `proxy` 两个预先存在的图片用例红(与本改动无关),config/pool/auth 全绿

body: ## Bug and impact Concurrent expense request submissions could receive the same mock request `id` because IDs were generated directly from `Date.now()`. A duplicated ID makes requests no longer independently addressable; later status updates by ID can mutate multiple requests and detail navigation can resolve the wrong row. ## Root cause `createRequest` used `String(Date.now())` after an async delay, so same-millisecond submissions shared the same identifier. ## Fix Added a monotonic ID generator that advances beyond both the current timestamp and the last generated ID, then switched `createRequest` to use it. Added a Vitest regression test that freezes `Date.now()`, creates two requests concurrently, and verifies updating one leaves the other unchanged. ## Validation - `npm test` - `npm run build`

- **Three call sites patched:** each `assert_contains(&files, ...)` → `assert_contains(files, ...)`

- No production code touched; this is test-only and behavior-invisible.

### Motivation

- Keep the main Chat de OS view focused on active, pending and paused services by hiding closed/finalized/canceled OS from operational lists. 
- Preserve full history and messages for audit while providing a separate, opt-in historical filter for closed OS.

### Description

- Restricts the operational chat queries to active statuses by adding `ACTIVE_OS_STATUSES` / `CLOSED_OS_STATUSES` and using them in `listarConversasOS` to return only active/non-archived OS by default and a separate history query when `filtro` is `finalizadas`/`historico` (`modules/os-chat/os-chat.service.js`).
- Adds automatic conversation archiving: when an OS becomes final (closed/finalized/concluded/canceled) the code records a system message `"Sistema: Ordem de Serviço encerrada em DD/MM/AAAA HH:MM. Conversa arquivada automaticamente."` and marks the OS row with `chat_arquivada = 1` and/or `status_chat = 'ARQUIVADO'` (preserves messages/attachments) and exposes `arquivarConversaOS(osId)` (`modules/os-chat/os-chat.service.js`).
- Integrates archiving into OS lifecycle: calls `arquivarConversaOS` from `concluirOS` and from `updateStatus` when status changes to a final state, and updates OS fields (`chat_arquivada` / `status_chat`) when status changes (without deleting messages) (`modules/os/os.service.js`).
- Adds a DB migration `161_os_chat_arquivamento.js` to create `chat_arquivada` and `status_chat` columns, an index `idx_os_chat_status_operacional` and to mark existing closed OS as archived (`database/migrations/161_os_chat_arquivamento.js`).
- UI and controller changes: introduces a separate `Finalizadas`/`Histórico` filter (not loaded by default) and a history display mode that shows `Número da OS`, `Equipamento`, `Responsável`, `Data de abertura`, `Data de fechamento` and `Última mensagem` when viewing archived OS (`modules/os-chat/os-chat.controller.js`, `views/os-chat/index.ejs`).
- Adjusts unread counters and `contarNaoLidas` so archived/closed OS are ignored in operational counts (`modules/os-chat/os-chat.service.js`).

### Testing

- Ran syntax checks: `node -c modules/os-chat/os-chat.service.js && node -c modules/os/os.service.js && node -c modules/os-chat/os-chat.controller.js && node -c database/migrations/161_os_chat_arquivamento.js` — all checked cleanly.
- Applied migrations locally with `npm run migrate` and the new migration ran successfully and backfilled `chat_arquivada`/`status_chat` for existing closed OS.
- Ran the test suite with `npm test`; most unit tests passed but the run failed due to missing environment dependencies in this execution environment (missing packages such as `pdfkit`, `web-push`, `express`), so full test verification could not be completed here.  All added code includes guards to remain compatible with older schemas when columns/tables are missing.
